_notes: One entry per running venue: 'port' is that venue's control.port, not its
FIX port. A venue that is down shows as disconnected and is redialled
automatically, so the order in which processes start does not matter.
'token' must match that venue's control.token when it sets one. The token
stays in this process; the browser never sees it.
Set allow_order_entry to false to serve a board that cannot trade, and
allow_market_control to false to serve one that cannot move a market
between phases. They are separate switches because they are different
powers: closing a market expires every resting order on it, other
clients' included. Both false is a read-only board.
allow_audit is a third switch, for the message audit view. It shows
every client's traffic, so a board that may not place an order should
not thereby be able to read everyone else's.
'board' is presentation, and grants nothing. 'buy_side' puts the buying
side of the ticket, the Level 1 quotes and the depth ladder all on one
side -- 'right' by default, which is where a Japanese board puts bids.
'left' moves all three together; they are never split, because a ticket
that disagreed with the ladder above it is a click waiting to go the
wrong way.
'buy_colour' and 'sell_colour' name a hue from the stylesheet's palette:
red, green, blue or amber. Each is defined for both the dark and the
light theme and each clears the 4.5:1 contrast floor in both, which is
why it is a name and not a colour value. The default pair is the
Japanese convention -- buying red, selling green -- which is the reverse
of the Western one. The two sides may not wear the same hue.
Both spellings, buy_colour and buy_color, are read.
